assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean theory-experiment pair: the continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle, followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. It opened an entire field of moire quantum matter with a tunable control parameter, and the many-body physics (strong correlations from geometry) is of the kind a statistical physicist finds compelling.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald supplied the decisive prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery of the correlated and superconducting phases. This maps naturally onto a theory-plus-experiment prize. Other experimental groups and other theorists (e.g. contemporaneous band-structure work) make a three-person allocation not entirely free of dispute.
assessment.maturity: Roughly seven to eight years since the key experiments, independently reproduced by many groups and across several moire platforms. The field is still moving, but the central discovery is stable and well confirmed.
uncertainties: Priority of the twist-angle idea among earlier band-structure work is judged from my own recollection, not verified here.
Mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is still debated, so a citation must be framed around flat-band correlated physics, not pairing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological classification of time-reversal-invariant insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect extended the topological idea of the 2016 prize into a new symmetry class and a broad program (topological materials, helical edge states). Conceptually clean, original and widely influential.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realization in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The BHZ theory and the Zhang group's role are a real complication since they are outside the supplied credit, and three-way credit is therefore only reasonably fair.
assessment.maturity: Nearly two decades of confirmation across 2D and 3D materials, with solid independent experiments. Timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The credit gap for the HgTe proposal (BHZ) cannot be resolved from the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phases prize may be viewed as reducing novelty by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated lattice models with ultracold atoms (superfluid-Mott transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy) lets one realize and probe many-body Hamiltonians that are intractable numerically. Important for many-body statistical physics and a major platform for quantum matter.
assessment.attribution: The theory proposal for the Bose-Hubbard realization is associated with Zoller and collaborators, the experimental observation of the Mott transition with Greiner, Bloch and Esslinger; Cirac is also a strong theory figure. With five credited names, any trio omits someone with a strong claim, so allocation is genuinely difficult.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of development, many independent groups, and increasingly quantitative results. Mature, though the field is evolving into programmable quantum simulation.
uncertainties: Which three of five credited names is fairest is unresolved; I am relying on recollection of who proposed versus who first demonstrated.
Part of the underlying cold-atom toolbox was already recognised by earlier prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The jamming picture unifies rigidity transitions in granular matter, foams, emulsions and glasses, with critical scaling and a role for isostaticity. It is a genuine statistical-physics idea with broad reach in disordered and soft matter, and is close in spirit to the complex-systems work I know best.
assessment.attribution: Liu and Nagel proposed the jamming phase diagram and drove the field; others (e.g. O'Hern, Silbert, Wyart and the mean-field glass community) contributed to the critical picture, so credit within the community is broader than two names, but a two-person prize is defensible.
assessment.maturity: About 25 years of simulation, experiment and theory, with detailed mean-field results in infinite dimensions. Mature as a concept, though the finite-dimensional critical theory is not fully settled.
uncertainties: Whether jamming is a true critical phase transition in finite dimensions is still debated.
Experimental verification is less sharp than for hardware-driven candidates, and the discovery is partly conceptual.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underpins the leading platform for solid-state quantum computing. High technological and scientific impact, and a controlled testbed for open quantum systems.
assessment.attribution: The Yale group (Schoelkopf experiment, Girvin and Blais theory) is a coherent core; Wallraff's early experimental demonstration is outside the supplied credit, which weakens fairness of this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Two decades old, strongly confirmed. The broader superconducting-circuit area was recognised in 2025, which affects timing and overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits may argue against a close follow-up.
The omission of key experimental contributors from the supplied credit list is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Intermittency and multifractality in fully developed turbulence are a central problem of nonequilibrium statistical physics. The conceptual and experimental contribution is real, but turbulence still lacks a closed theory, so the achievement is a framework and measurements rather than a solved problem.
assessment.attribution: Frisch (multifractal and phenomenological theory) and Sreenivasan (experimental scaling and intermittency) are credible. Parisi and Frisch's multifractal model and Kolmogorov's 1962 refinement predate them, and Benzi and others contributed, so priority is clouded.
assessment.maturity: Decades of data, but the interpretation (anomalous scaling exponents, universality) remains incomplete. I declare my own field's closeness and so treat this with caution and rank it below the more decisive discoveries.
uncertainties: Absence of a first-principles derivation of anomalous exponents.
Priority questions around the multifractal model and Kolmogorov 1962.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Renormalization-group theory of depinning and the universal scaling of avalanches (Barkhausen noise, earthquakes-like statistics) provides a general account of crackling noise in driven disordered systems. Elegant and broadly applicable, though its quantitative impact beyond a specialised community is moderate.
assessment.attribution: Fisher's depinning RG and Sethna's work on crackling noise and Barkhausen avalanches are the most decisive; Dahmen contributed to the universal scaling-function programme. Two-person allocation is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Established in theory and tested against several experiments, though quantitative agreement across systems varies.
uncertainties: Experimental confirmation of universality classes is mixed.
Broader recognition and impact are narrower than for the leading candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached 10^-18 fractional precision, from Katori's magic-wavelength lattice idea to Ye's record stability. A leading precision-measurement achievement with applications from geodesy to tests of fundamental constants and a prospective redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength optical lattice clock and Ye brought it to extreme precision; this is a clear two-person configuration. Others working on ion clocks and the comb are covered by earlier recognition.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple independent labs, with international comparisons. Mature, and the redefinition of the second is pending.
uncertainties: It may be viewed as an incremental extension of the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes.
Whether the redefinition of the second will occur on a timescale that affects the timing of recognition.
